name: Zechariah
overview: Zechariah is a male descendant of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as a descendant of Shecaniah. He is noted as a Levite whom Ezra sent to Iddo, possibly indicating a familial connection to Iddo, who may be his grandfather. Beyond these genealogical details, Scripture provides limited additional information about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Zechariah means 'y-h-v-h remembers,' reflecting the Hebrew understanding of God's faithfulness and remembrance. This proper name is recorded twice in Ezra 8:3 and 8:16, emphasizing the same meaning without indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Zechariah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe of Israel. He is also connected to Shecaniah, from whom he descends, and possibly to Iddo, to whom he was sent by Ezra. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Zechariah's significance lies in his role as a Levite during the post-exilic period, serving under Ezra's leadership. His identification as a descendant of Shecaniah and his involvement in the mission to Iddo highlight the restoration and reestablishment of the Levites' duties in Israel after the exile. This situates him within the broader narrative of God's faithfulness in preserving and remembering His covenant people, as reflected in his name.
